title: Rethinking Evaluation for Principled Generalization Using a Kripkean Challenge to Meaning as Use
abstract: arXiv:2610.35111v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models operationalize an intuitive, view of meaning as use. We argue that it faces a rule-following challenge. Using Kripke's interpretation of Wittgenstein, we argue that finite histories of use do not determine a unique rule for future extension. This reframes the debate about OOD generalization but also about NLP evaluation; benchmarks that measure performance on fixed use cases or local robustness, we argue, do not by themselves establish semantic competence. To evaluate whether models preserve rules and concepts under principled domain extension, we propose to evaluate two capacities, central to this ability: abstraction and recursion; and we offer an experimental paradigm for testing both.

translated_title: 基于克里普克对“意义即使用”的挑战，重新思考原则性泛化的评估
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型将“意义即使用”这一直观观点付诸操作化实践。我们认为这一观点面临着“遵循规则”的挑战。借助克里普克对维特根斯坦的解读，我们论证有限的使用历史并不能为未来的扩展确定唯一的规则。这不仅重新构建了关于分布外（OOD）泛化的争论，也重新构建了关于自然语言处理（NLP）评估的讨论；我们认为，那些衡量模型在固定使用案例上的表现或局部鲁棒性的基准测试，其本身并不能确立模型的语义能力。为了评估模型在原则性的领域扩展下是否能够保持规则和概念，我们提出评估两种对这一能力至关重要的能力：抽象与递归；并提供了一个用于测试这两种能力的实验范式。
tldr: 该论文借助克里普克对维特根斯坦的解读，论证有限的使用历史无法唯一确定规则，因此基于固定用例或局部鲁棒性的基准测试不足以证明语义能力，并提出通过评估抽象与递归两种能力来检验模型在原则性领域扩展下保持规则与概念的能力。
en_tdlr: Drawing on Kripke's reading of Wittgenstein, this paper argues that finite histories of use do not determine a unique rule, so benchmarks based on fixed use cases or local robustness cannot by themselves establish semantic competence, and proposes evaluating abstraction and recursion as central capacities for testing whether models preserve rules and concepts under principled domain extension.
